title: Coefficient cocycle for the proper direct-image mate
statement:
For arbitrary schemes, finite commutative coefficient rings A, B, C and ring homomorphisms phi:A→B and psi:B→C, the canonical comparisons satisfy the following equation, with no boundedness, constructibility or properness assumptions. The functors and normalized associators are those of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] and [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison].

theorem directImageScalarCoefficientCocycle
    {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Finite A] [Finite B] [Finite C] (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C)
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : Z ⟶ Y) (N : proEtaleDerivedCategory Z A) :
    (scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Y).hom.app
        ((directImageConstantPush A p).obj N) ≫
      (directImageScalarComparison (ψ.comp φ) p).app N =
    (scalarExtensionFunctor ψ Y).map ((directImageScalarComparison φ p).app N) ≫
      (directImageScalarComparison ψ p).app ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ Z).obj N) ≫
        (directImageConstantPush C p).map
          ((scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Z).hom.app N)

proof.text: Apply the C-linear adjunction bijection to both coefficient composites. The defining mate/counit identity transforms the direct comparison to scalar extension of the A-counit. For the successive comparison use naturality of the C-counit, the B-to-C mate identity, naturality of the tensor/pullback comparison at the A-to-B mate, and then its mate identity. The tensor/pullback coefficient cocycle identifies the resulting first factors, and naturality of the coefficient associator at the A-counit identifies the last factors. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives equality. This calculation is the proved private lemma mate_cocycle in the delivered module.

proof_origin.place: Expanded Step 10: formal mate calculation in Lean, reducing only the tensor/pullback normalization
